scope: Corollary 3.3 (Integrated level weights) of the manuscript “An exact Hausdorff gauge for SLE” (preprints/An-exact-Hausdorff-gauge-for-SLE-September-25-2026/An-exact-Hausdorff-gauge-for-SLE-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 230 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 513ca9aedce0f342), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let f ≥ 0 be bounded and supported in a compact K ⋐ D. Then, for every integer m ≥ 1, sup l>0 E[Al(f)m ] < ∞. (3.15) Fix also x0 ∈ D and 0 < e0 ≤ RD(x0), and let E0 be the event that x0 reaches radius e0 while alive. Then sup l>0 E[1E0 Al(f)m ] ≤ Ceα 0 . (3.16) Here C can be chosen using only m, a, the size and support of f, the bounded location of x0, and a positive lower bound for RD on K ∪ {x0}. In particular, in a fixed disk these bounds are uniform over all initial boundary angles.
